_note: Every surface the brand ships to, and which generated plate it is cut from. 'plate' names a format in prompts.json. 'mode' is 'cover' (fill the frame, trim the rest) or 'fit' (scale the whole composition down and pad with the plate's own paper). Use 'cover' by default. Use 'fit' only when the surface ratio is CLOSE to the plate's, where the padding reads as a margin - at an extreme gap it shrinks the art to a stamp, and the answer there is a new generation brief, not a different crop. 'focus' is the vertical anchor of a cover crop, 0 top, 1 bottom.

github-social.use: GitHub repository social preview. Settings, Social preview. Must stay under 1 MB.

og.use: Open Graph and Twitter card. Link previews in chat, Slack, search.

readme-banner.use: The wide strip at the top of a README. Its own panoramic composition, layered edge to edge.

linkedin-banner.use: LinkedIn company page cover. Cut from the ultrawide frieze, whose elements march across a shallow centre strip so a 5.9:1 crop stays dense.

linkedin-post.use: LinkedIn link post and single-image post.

x-header.use: X profile header. Its own bold composition: one large amber field, the cup reversed out, high contrast. Centre is safe, edges are overlaid by the UI.

instagram-square.use: Square social post. Centred poster with the stacked two-line lockup and the cup as hero.

story.use: Stories and reels cover. Cut from the portrait stack, briefed with side margins so the 9:16 crop never clips the name.

email-header.use: Newsletter header. Its own editorial composition: type-led, one amber diagonal, a stack of notes.

print-a4-landscape.use: A4 at 300 dpi, for a poster by the machine or a one-pager cover. Upscaled from the plate, so check it at size before printing.
